source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture / ASPIRE program - Technical Document: "Sweet Corn Cultivation Techniques Resilient to Climate Change" (បច្ចេកទេសដាំដាំណាំពោតផ្អែមធន់នឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ), 2018
text:
Land preparation and bed forming: plow and leave the soil to dry/fallow for 10-15 days. Plow a second time, harrow the soil finely, and remove all weeds/grass before forming planting beds. Form beds 1 meter wide and 20-30 cm high (or 2-3 hoe-blade heights), leaving a 0.5 meter gap between beds; then dig a furrow along the length of each bed to hold base fertilizer. Apply animal manure or compost along the furrow the length of the bed, then cover the soil back over it — this helps enrich the soil, loosens the soil, increases beneficial soil insects, promotes plant growth, reduces harmful pests and crop disease, and helps retain soil moisture to withstand drought caused by climate change. Cover the bed with plastic mulch or rice straw/dried grass to retain soil moisture and prevent weed growth.

Planting can be done by two methods: direct seeding, or raising seedlings first and then transplanting.

Direct seeding: before planting, soak the seed in water for 4-6 hours. Then take the soaked seed and mix it with a fungicide seed treatment (mix 300 grams of fungicide powder with 100 kg of dry corn seed) to protect against fungal disease. Plant with 35-45 cm spacing between hills (or 3.5-4.5 hoe-blades), placing only 1 seed per hill, and bury the seed 2-3 cm deep.

Raising seedlings then transplanting: for the seedling mix, combine 1 part fine compost, 1 part ordinary soil, and 2 parts rice-husk charcoal, mix thoroughly, moisten with water until damp, then let it rest covered for 2 days. Sterilize the soil mix by steaming for 45-60 minutes, let it cool, then fill seedling trays with it. Push the corn seed into the tray hole to a depth of 2.5 times the seed's own size, water gently, then cover the bag/tray to keep it closed. Check diligently (3 times a day); once seedlings emerge, remove them from the enclosed bag and place them on a shelf that has some shade cover. To transplant: form hills at the same spacing used for direct seeding; use a stick to poke a planting hole in the bed, or use a mechanical hole-punch/plastic-mulch hole-maker to make holes evenly spaced along the row per the planned hill spacing; pour water into the hole; gently remove the young corn seedling and place it in the hole, then firm the soil around the base.
